query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating microstructural modeling of dynamic amorphization and nanocrystalline layer formation into predictive methods will improve the accuracy of identifying high-entropy alloys that have low phonon thermal conductivity compared to conventional ab initio or bulk-averaging approaches.
generation.material_initial_state: Single‐phase high-entropy alloys (e.g., CoCrFeMnNi) synthesized in a coarse-grained state where grain size and boundary characteristics can be controlled.
generation.intervention: Apply a predictive approach that explicitly incorporates the effects of grain boundary dynamics and dynamic amorphization (leading to nanocrystalline near-surface layers) into thermal conductivity models.
generation.conditions: Measurements performed under controlled conditions (e.g., ultra-high vacuum to limit oxidation) with systematic variation in grain size to capture transitions from coarse to ultra-nanocrystalline states.
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundaries and the formation of dynamically induced ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layers, which are expected to serve as effective phonon scattering centers.
generation.mechanism: The approach works by correlating increased grain boundary density and the presence of dynamic amorphized regions with enhanced phonon scattering, thereby reducing phonon mean free paths and, consequently, the thermal conductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: High-entropy alloys identified using this approach will show measured phonon thermal conductivities that are approximately 10–20% lower than those predicted by traditional ab initio methods that do not account for microstructural dynamics.
generation.baseline: Traditional predictive models for phonon thermal conductivity that rely on bulk material properties and ab initio calculations without explicit consideration of evolving microstructural features such as dynamic amorphization.
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of the predictive approach will be limited to single-phase HEAs with controllable grain structures; systems that are multiphase or where oxidation and extrinsic surface effects dominate may not exhibit the predicted improvements.
generation.uncertainty: The predicted improvement (10–20% lower thermal conductivity) is approximate and may vary with alloy composition, processing conditions, and the extent of dynamic amorphization. The direct correlation between the observed microstructural features and phonon transport requires further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloys with systematically varied grain sizes. Under ultra-high vacuum, characterize the samples using STEM and in situ TEM to quantify grain boundary densities and detect the formation of dynamic amorphous near-surface layers. Simultaneously, measure the phonon thermal conductivity using laser flash analysis.
measurements: Grain size and boundary density via STEM
Detection of amorphous layers via in situ TEM
Phonon thermal conductivity via laser flash measurement
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured thermal conductivity of alloys does not show a statistically significant (≥10%) reduction compared to predictions from conventional models, or if no clear correlation is found between enhanced phonon scattering (as per microstructural features) and lower thermal conductivity, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Evidence of Inverse Hall-Petch Behavior and Low Friction and Wear in High Entropy Alloys

Abstract: AbstractWe present evidence of inverse Hall-Petch behavior for a single-phase high entropy alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) in ultra-high vacuum and show that it is associated with low friction coefficients (~0.3). Grain size measurements by STEM validate a recently proposed dynamic amorphization model that accurately predicts grain size-dependent shear strength in the inverse Hall-Petch regime. Wear rates in the initially soft (coarse grained) material were shown to be remarkably low (~10–6 mm3/N-m), the lowest for any HEA tested in an inert environment where oxidation and the formation of mixed metal-oxide films is mitigated. The combined high wear resistance and low friction are linked to the formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer. The dynamic amorphization model was also used to predict an average high angle grain boundary energy (0.87 J/m2). This value was used to explain cavitation-induced nanoporosity found in the highly deformed surface layer, a phenomenon that has been linked to superplasticity.Subject terms: Structural materials, Structural properties
